</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><b>INTRODUCTORY NOTE</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">OSR Holdings, Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a global healthcare
company dedicated to advancing healthcare outcomes and improving the quality of life for people and their families. We aim to build and
develop a robust portfolio of innovative and potentially transformative therapies and healthcare solutions. Our current operating businesses
(through our three wholly owned&#160;subsidiaries) include (i)&#160;developing oral immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer, (ii)&#160;developing
design-augmented&#160;biologics for age-related&#160;and other degenerative diseases and (iii)&#160;neurovascular intervention medical
device and systems distribution in Korea. The Company&#8217;s vision is to acquire and operate a portfolio of innovative healthcare-related
companies globally.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Prior to the closing of our initial business combination on February
14, 2025 (the &#8220;Closing&#8221;) comprising the merger via share exchange of the Company and our target company OSR Holdings, Co.,
Ltd. a corporation organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea (&#8220;OSR&#8221;), previously reported on Form 8-K filed February
14, 2025 and further described below, the Company operated as a blank check company under the name Bellevue Life Sciences Acquisition
Corp.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Unless the context indicates otherwise, references in this report to
&#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221; means the OSR Holdings, Inc. and our consolidated subsidiaries, and refer
to the historical operations of the Company under the name of Bellevue Life Sciences Acquisition Corp. prior to the Closing (sometimes
referred to herein as &#8220;<i>BLAC</i>&#8221;) and to the combined OSR Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries following the Closing. References
to &#8220;<i>OSR</i>&#8221; refer to the legacy historical operations of OSR Holdings, Ltd. and its subsidiaries prior to the Closing.
References to our &#8220;management&#8221; or our &#8220;management team&#8221; refer to our officers and directors, and references to
the &#8220;Sponsor&#8221; refer to Bellevue Global Life Sciences Investors LLC, a Delaware limited liability company.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">This Annual Report on Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December
31, 2025, and presents the consolidated results of OSR Holdings, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries for that fiscal year.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The Company was formed as a Delaware corporation on February&#160;25,
2020, for the purpose of entering into a merger, share exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, recapitalization, reorganization or
similar business combination with one or more businesses.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On February&#160;14, 2023, we consummated our initial public offering
(&#8220;<i>IPO</i>&#8221;) of an aggregate of 6,000,000 units, at $10.00 per unit (&#8220;<i>Units</i>&#8221;), generating gross proceeds
of $60,000,000 before underwriting discounts and expenses.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Simultaneously with the closing of our IPO, our sponsor, Bellevue Global
Life Sciences Investors, LLC (&#8220;<i>Sponsor</i>&#8221;), purchased an aggregate of 430,000 units at a price of $10.00 per unit, for
an aggregate purchase price of $4,300,000 (&#8220;Private Placement Units&#8221;).</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">In connection with our IPO, the underwriters were granted a 45-day
option from the date of our prospectus issued in connection with our IPO (the &#8220;<i>Over-Allotment Option</i>&#8221;) to purchase
up to 900,000 additional units to cover over-allotments (the &#8220;<i>Over-Allotment Units</i>&#8221;), if any. On February&#160;21,
2023, the underwriters purchased 900,000 Over-Allotment Units fully exercising the Over-Allotment Option. The Over-Allotment Units were
sold at an offering price of $10.00 per Over-Allotment Unit, generating additional gross proceeds of $9,000,000 to the Company.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>


</div><!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 2 --><div>
    </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></div><div>
    </div><div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><p style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"></p></div><div>
    </div><!-- Field: /Page --><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The transaction costs of our IPO amounted to $2,721,126, consisting
of $1,380,000 of underwriting discounts and $1,341,126 of other offering costs. Following the closing of our IPO on February&#160;14,
2023, $61,050,000 (approximately $10.175 per Unit) from net offering proceeds of the sale of the Units in our IPO and the sale of the
Private Placement Units was placed in a trust account (the &#8220;<i>Trust Account</i>&#8221;). Following the closing of the Over-Allotment
Option on February&#160;21, 2023, and including the amount from our IPO, an aggregate amount of $70,207,500 was placed in the Company&#8217;s
Trust Account established in connection with our IPO. The proceeds held in the Trust Account are invested in United States &#8220;government
securities&#8221; within the meaning of Section&#160;2(a)(16) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the &#8220;<i>Investment
Company Act</i>&#8221;) having a maturity of 185 days or less or in money market funds meeting certain conditions under Rule 2a-7 promulgated
under the Investment Company Act which invest only in direct U.S. government treasury obligations. Except with respect to interest earned
on the funds held in the Trust Account that may be released to the Company to pay its tax obligations, the proceeds from our IPO were
not to be released from the Trust Account until the earlier of: (a)&#160;the completion of the Company&#8217;s initial business combination,
(b)&#160;the redemption of any of our public shares properly submitted in connection with a stockholder vote to amend our Amended and
Restated Certificate of Incorporation (the &#8220;<i>Charter</i>&#8221;) (1) to modify the substance or timing of our obligation to allow
redemption in connection with our initial business combination or to redeem 100% of our public shares if we do not complete our initial
business combination within the time provided in the Company&#8217;s Charter (as subject to extension), or (2)&#160;with respect to any
other provision relating to stockholders&#8217; rights or pre-initial business combination activity; or (c)&#160;absent an initial business
combination within the time provided in the Company&#8217;s Charter (as subject to extension), our return of the funds held in the Trust
Account to our public stockholders as part of our redemption of the public shares. &#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On March&#160;14, 2023, the Company announced that, commencing on March&#160;17,
2023, the holders of Units may elect to separately trade the shares of common stock, warrants and rights included in the Units. No fractional
shares, warrants or rights would be issued upon separation of the Units and only whole shares, warrants and rights would trade. The shares
of common stock, the warrants and the rights traded on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbols &#8220;BLAC,&#8221; &#8220;BLACW&#8221;
and &#8220;BLACR,&#8221; respectively, and the Units not separated continued to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol &#8220;BLACU&#8221;
until the closing of our initial business combination on February 14, 2025 as discussed below.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The Company and OSR entered into a Business Combination Agreement dated
November&#160;16, 2023 (the &#8220;<i>Business Combination Agreement</i>&#8221;) pursuant to which, prior to the Closing each holder of
OSR Common Stock that executes a Participating Stockholder Joinder to the Business Combination Agreement on or prior to the Closing (each
such Person, a &#8220;<i>Participating OSR Stockholder</i>&#8221;), and each holder of OSR Common Stock that executes a&#160;Non-Participating&#160;Stockholder
Joinder on or prior to the Closing (each such Person, a &#8220;<i>Non-Participating&#160;OSR Stockholder</i>&#8221;) would be joined as
parties to the Business Combination Agreement, pursuant to which at the Effective Time (i)&#160;the Company would issue the Aggregate
Participating Consideration to the Participating OSR Stockholders, and (ii)&#160;the Participating OSR Stockholders would sell, transfer,
convey, assign and deliver all of their respective shares of OSR Common Stock to the Company (subclauses (i)&#160;and (ii), collectively,
the &#8220;<i>Share Exchange</i>&#8221;).</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">As previously disclosed on the Company&#8217;s Current Report filed
on Form 8-K on February 21, 2025, on February 14, 2025 (the &#8220;<i>Closing Date</i>&#8221;), the Company completed its previously announced
business combination (the &#8220;<i>Business Combination</i>&#8221;) with OSR pursuant to the Amended and Restated Business Combination
Agreement, dated as of May&#160;23, 2024, as amended on December&#160;20, 2024 (the &#8220;<i>Business Combination Agreement</i>&#8221;),
by and among the Company, OSR, each stockholder of OSR that executed a Participating Joinder thereto (each such person, a &#8220;<i>Participating
Stockholder</i>&#8221;), and each stockholder of OSR that executed a Non-Participating Joinder thereto (each such person, a &#8220;<i>Non-Participating
Stockholder</i>&#8221;, and together with the Participating Stockholders, the &#8220;<i>OSR Stockholders</i>&#8221;). As a subsequent
event following the end of the period covered by this Form 10-K, the Non-Participating Stockholders exercised their options to put their
OSR shares to exchange them into the shares of the common stock of OSR Holdings, Inc. The effective date of the closing of such share
exchange with the Non-Participating Stockholders was January 30, 2026</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">In connection with the Closing of the Business Combination, we changed
our name from Bellevue Life Sciences Acquisition Corp. to OSR Holdings, Inc. and changed the trading symbols of our common stock and warrants
from &#8220;BLAC&#8221; and &#8220;BLACW,&#8221; to &#8220;OSRH&#8221; and &#8220;OSRHW,&#8221; respectively. In connection with the Closing,
any Units (which were trading under the symbol &#8220;BLACU&#8221;) that had not yet separated, were separated into their component shares
of common stock and warrants and ceased trading.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><b>SUMMARY OF RISK FACTORS</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Our business, our business sector and investing in our securities involve
a number of risks of which you should be aware before making an investment decision. You should read this summary together with the description
of each risk factor contained under &#8220;Item IA. Risk&#160;Factors&#8221; in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, as well as other documents
filed from time to time with the SEC, for a more detailed discussion of certain risks that could materially adversely affect our financial
conditions and the market price of our securities. The following list describes some of the principal risk factors applicable to the Business
Combination, BLAC, OSR and the combined Company.</p><div>

</div><div><a id="a_001"></a></div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><b>PART I </b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><div><a id="a_002"></a></div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Item 1. Business </b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Company and Business Strategy Overview</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">As a global healthcare holding company, with operations in South Korea
and Switzerland and an office in the United&#160;States, we intend to leverage our existing and expanding network of academic and industry
leaders and investor network, including venture capital and private equity, in major healthcare markets globally to identify, lead and
support the growth of our subsidiaries and subsidiary candidates based on innovative research. Subsidiary candidates are companies that
are either already existing entities or new companies formed in connection with acquiring or licensing existing assets from industry or
academia. We expect to attract industry partners either as co-investors&#160;or through technology licensing deals and may raise capital
directly from private, strategic or public investors. We seek to chart a potentially more efficient and optimal route by pairing what
we believe are the right team and pharmaceutical or medical device technologies that have the potential to treat diseases and improve
healthcare outcomes with the necessary financial and other resources. Since our target markets feature large established global businesses
with abundant capital that acquire healthcare companies, we hope to realize additional liquidity through the sale of our subsidiaries
from time to time.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">We are a data-driven&#160;company. We evaluate our subsidiary candidate
opportunities by better understanding the target indications toward identifying new approaches and technologies to improve treatment outcomes.
We collaborate with academic and industry leaders to promote a seamless integration and partnership between entrepreneurial scientists
and seasoned business development and leadership teams. These technical and scientific experts from academia and industry bring innovative
contributions and a high level of enthusiasm. Our holding company leadership team supports and empowers each subsidiary to transform their
potentially breakthrough discoveries into impactful and viable commercial products.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Our company&#8217;s collective expertise from industry veterans, seasoned
scientists, capital market and legal professionals provides the core foundation of our global healthcare holding company. The Company
operates as a hub-and-spoke&#160;business model with a centralized executive team partnering with subsidiary management teams to ensure
overall program and corporate alignment by and between subsidiaries and holding company. Our overarching goal is to enhance value creation
for our subsidiaries by continuously assessing optimal development options and exploring partnership and fundraising opportunities. We
encourage cooperation and knowledge sharing among our subsidiaries to enhance our synergistic business model. We believe our strong foundational
scientific conviction, entrepreneurial acumen and opportunistic approach positions us as a differentiated global company advancing pharmaceutical
and medical device technologies in an efficient, cost-effective&#160;and meaningful manner. Our interdisciplinary team of accomplished
scientists and entrepreneurial business leaders promotes the development and commercialization of a risk diversified portfolio to address
unmet medical needs with resilience and efficiency.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

by the following chart*:</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Portfolio Overview</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">OSR&#8217;s subsidiaries (other than RMC) have diverse scientific and
technological developments, and are engaged in distinct areas of therapeutics research and development, including oral T-cell&#160;immunotherapies
and recombinant biologics. This approach not only provides the Company with a broader scope of potential therapeutic solutions but also
reduces the risks associated with a singular-asset&#160;approach.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Individual patents are in force for varying periods of time, depending
upon the date of filing of the patent application, the date of patent issuance, and the legal term of patents in the countries in which
they are obtained. Generally, patents issued for applications filed in the United&#160;States are in force for 20&#160;years from the
earliest nonprovisional filing date. In addition, in certain instances, a patent term can be adjusted or extended to recapture a portion
of the term effectively lost as a result of the USPTO delay or the FDA regulatory review period (a patent term adjustment or patent term
extension, respectively). The restoration period for FDA delay cannot be longer than five&#160;years and the total patent term, including
the restoration period, must not exceed 14&#160;years following FDA approval. The duration of patents outside of the United&#160;States
varies in accordance with provisions of applicable local law, but typically is also 20&#160;years from the earliest nonprovisional filing
date. However, the actual protection afforded by a patent varies on a product-by-product&#160;basis, from country-to-country, and depends
upon many factors, including the type of patent, the scope of its coverage, the availability of regulatory-related&#160;extensions, the
availability of legal remedies in a particular country, and the validity and enforceability of the patent.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Vaximm</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Vaximm Corporate Overview</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Vaximm is developing innovative oral T-cell immunotherapies for the
treatment of disorders that require the safe and targeted elimination of specific cell populations. (e.g. neoplasms, other proliferative
diseases, chronic infections). Based on over 20&#160;years of research, Vaximm&#8217;s customizable immunotherapy platform has the potential
to be efficiently and effectively adapted to treat various diseases and address specific patient needs. Vaximm currently has three clinical
and pre-clinical&#160;drug candidates targeting diseases ranging from glioblastoma to gastrointestinal stromal tumor to ocular diseases.
Vaximm holds the only clinically tested oral cancer vaccine with proven safety and demonstrated efficacy</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Vaximm&#8217;s flagship asset, VXM01, is a late
clinical-stage&#160;(NCT037500701) immuno-oncology&#160;candidate for glioblastoma, which early-stage&#160;clinical trials
(NCT02718443 and NCT01486329) suggest may be a potentially specific and effective treatment. VXM01 has been granted Orphan Drug
Designation by the U.S.&#160;Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA) for both glioblastoma and
pancreatic cancer on August&#160;31, 2017 from FDA and August&#160;23, 2017 from EMA.&#160;An Orphan Drug Designation will permit
Vaximm to receive additional&#160;years of market exclusivity upon regulatory approval, which provides a significant competitive
advantage. See &#8220;<i>Government Regulation</i>&#160;<i>&#8212;&#160;Orphan Drug Designation and Exclusivity</i>.&#8221; &#8220;
Based on evolving science, Vaximm is developing the VXM01 v 2.0. While meant to improve efficacy, it leverages the proven vector
safety data from VXM01 to move into late-stage development at speed.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">While VXM01 (including version 2.0) moves into planned phase 2, phase
2/3 clinical trials, we are continuing to evaluate Vaximm&#8217;s other preclinical candidates for further development in investigational
new drug (IND)-enabling&#160;studies.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Importantly, the live, attenuated <i>S.</i> typhi strain Ty21a, presents
a proprietary platform for inducing an immune response to other antigens beyond the here chosen VEGFR-2, such as Carcinoembryonic Antigen
(CEA), Fibroblast Activation Protein (FAP) expressed in the tumor stroma, or Multiple Drug Resistance 1 (MDR-1). We have since tested
in preclinical models a variety of other antigens with success.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 48pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">These products are currently undergoing preclinical studies to evaluate
their safety, immunogenicity, and anti-tumor&#160;efficacy. Vaximm will need to complete these preclinical studies and submit Investigational
New Drug (IND) applications to the relevant regulatory authorities before initiating clinical trials for each of these product candidates.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">While Vaximm has direct experience advancing a therapeutic candidate
from preclinical to late-stage&#160;clinical trials and developed a pipeline of other preclinical therapeutic candidates, other than receiving
Orphan Drug Designation for VXMO1, Vaximm has limited experience in applying for regulatory or marketing approval for any of its product
candidates specifically. That said, this experience exists within the team. As Vaximm continues to advance its line of oral immunotherapies,
it will remain flexible and opportunistic to explore partnering options.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

    </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->4<!-- Field: /Sequence --></p></div><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Opportunity</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Current approaches to targeted immunotherapies have various limitations,
such as drug biodistribution, off-target&#160;effects, immunotolerance, and evasion. The complex and diverse makeup of tumor microenvironments
creates further difficulties. Production of targeted immunotherapies is expensive and time-intensive, making tailor-made&#160;therapies
challenging to produce and manufacture at scale and, thus, not readily accessible. Optimally, the development of innovative new strategies
can overcome drug resistance, enhance druggability, and improve drug biodistribution to maximize treatment efficacy.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Vaximm seeks to overcome these limitations by leveraging our foundational
science and innovative platform of attenuated bacterial strains to produce effective, customizable, oral vaccines efficiently and cost-effectively.
Vaximm&#8217;s lead product candidate, VXM01, targets the tumor vasculature and specific tumor antigens. It differs decidedly from other
vaccine approaches, since VXM01 does not have to overcome local immune suppression/encapsulation. The target, further, does not allow
for mutations and immune escape. VXM01 and the underlying proprietary platform, further, has the potential to target multiple indications,
even beyond oncology.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">VXM01 has recently completed a Phase&#160;2 clinical trial in Europe
for the treatment of recurrent glioblastoma, where activity has been observed to date. Vaximm also plans to initiate a new clinical trial
of VXM01 in recurrent glioblastoma patients in the United&#160;States.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">If VXM01 demonstrates efficacy in the treatment of recurrent glioblastoma,
Vaximm intends to expand by developing oral cancer vaccines targeting other solid tumor indications. The company&#8217;s strategy generally
involves the following key steps:</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 48pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.25in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">1.</span></td>
    <td>
    <p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Identify novel tumor-specific&#160;antigens: Vaximm will leverage its
    expertise in antigen discovery to identify new tumor-specific&#160;antigens that can be targeted by Vaximm&#8217;s platform. This will
    include, as per precedent, targets which are expressed by cancer supporting tissue.</p>
    <p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The safety profile and the mode of action of the platform make it a
    prime candidate for combination with standard of care treatments. Thus, currently envisioned clinical development will initially focus
    on add-on trials, avoiding initially combinations of non-approved assets. This presents a straight forward way to approval.</p></td></tr>
  </table><div>
</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 48pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.25in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">2.</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Conduct preclinical studies with the FDA&#8217;s good laboratory practice (&#8220;GLP&#8221; regulations): Before testing any drug or biological product candidate in humans, the product candidate must undergo rigorous pre-clinical&#160;testing. The pre-clinical&#160;developmental stage generally involves laboratory evaluations of drug chemistry, formulation, and stability, as well as studies to evaluate toxicity in animals, to assess the potential for adverse events and, in some cases, to establish a rationale for therapeutic use. The conduct of pre-clinical&#160;studies is subject to federal regulations and requirements, including GLP regulations for safety/toxicology studies. Vaximm will perform preclinical studies to evaluate the safety, immunogenicity, and anti-tumor&#160;efficacy of its oral cancer vaccine candidates in line with the GLP regulations that the FDA requires.</span></td></tr>
  </table><div>
</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 48pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.25in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">3.</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">File an Investigational New Drug (IND) application: Upon the successful completion of preclinical studies, Vaximm will submit an IND application to regulatory authorities such as the FDA.&#160;IND is a request for authorization from the FDA to ship an investigation product and then administer it to humans and must be allowed to proceed by the FDA before human clinical trials may begin. This submission includes all relevant data from preclinical studies and outlines the proposed clinical trial protocols. The IND review period typically takes 30&#160;days, during which the regulatory agency evaluates the submission to ensure the safety of proceeding to human trials.</span></td></tr>
  </table><div>
</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 48pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">

    <td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Initiate clinical trials: Based on the preclinical data and IND approval, the company will design and conduct additional Phase&#160;2 clinical trials to assess the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of its oral cancer vaccines in other cancer indications.</span></td></tr>
  </table><div>

    <td style="width: 0.25in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">6.</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Seek regulatory approval: Following the successful completion of Phase&#160;3 clinical trials, the result of the pre-clinical&#160;studies and clinical trials, together with detailed information relating to the product&#8217;s chemistry, manufacture, controls, and proposed labeling, among other things, are submitted to authorities, such as the FDA or EMA.&#160;This stage is known as the New Drug Application (NDA) review.</span></td></tr>
  </table><div>
</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Regulatory Steps</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>New Drug Application</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="text-align: left; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">A New Drug Application (NDA) tells the full story of a drug. Its purpose
is to demonstrate that a drug is safe and effective for its intended use in the population studied.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">A drug developer must include everything about a drug&#160;&#8212;&#160;from
preclinical data to Phase&#160;3 trial data&#160;&#8212;&#160;in an NDA.&#160;Developers must include reports on all studies, data, and
analyses. Along with clinical results, developers must include proposed labeling, safety updates, drug abuse information, patent information,
any data from studies that may have been conducted in other countries, institutional review board compliance information and directions
for use. Vaximm has that information largely readily available due to past work. Especially, there seems no need for expensive and long-lasting
animal safety studies.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>NDA Review</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Once each authority such as FDA or EMA receives an NDA, the review
team decides if it is complete. If it is not complete, the review team can refuse to file the NDA.&#160;If it is complete, the review
team has 6 to 10&#160;months to make a decision on whether to approve the drug. The process includes the following:</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 48pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.25in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Each member of the review team conducts a full review of his or her section of the application. For example, the medical officer and the statistician review clinical data, while a pharmacologist reviews the data from animal studies. Within each technical discipline represented on the team, there is also a supervisory review. All expertise needed with a proven track record are available within the team</span></td></tr>
  </table><div>
</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 48pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.25in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">FDA or EMA inspectors travel to clinical study sites to conduct a routine inspection. The Agency looks for evidence of fabrication, manipulation, or withholding of data.</span></td></tr>
  </table><div>
</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 48pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.25in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The project manager assembles all individual reviews and other documents, such as the inspection report, into an &#8220;action package.&#8221; This document becomes the record for NDA review. The review team issues a recommendation, and a senior official makes a decision.</span></td></tr>
  </table><div>
</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>NDA Approval</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">In cases where FDA or EMA determines that a drug has been shown to
be safe and effective for its intended use, it is then necessary to work with the applicant to develop and refine prescribing information.
This is referred to as &#8220;labeling.&#8221; Labeling accurately and objectively describes the basis for approval and how best to use
the drug.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

</div><!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 13; Value: 1 --><div>
    </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->6<!-- Field: /Sequence --></p></div><div>
    </div><div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><p style="margin: 0pt"></p></div><div>
    </div><!-- Field: /Page --><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>FDA Advisory Committees</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Often, the NDA contains sufficient data for FDA or EMA to determine
the safety and effectiveness of a drug. Sometimes, though, questions arise that require additional consideration. In these cases, FDA
or EMA may organize a meeting of one of its Advisory Committees to get independent, expert advice and to permit the public to make comments.
These Advisory Committees include a Patient Representative that provides input from the patient perspective.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The estimated timeframe for this process is as follows:</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">VXM01 was clinically tested in two trials in advanced pancreatic cancer
and in Glioblastoma:</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 44pt; text-indent: -22pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-indent: -0.25in"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>VXM01 Phase I Dose Escalation Study in Patients With Locally Advanced,
Inoperable and Stage IV Pancreatic Cancer.</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">NCT01486329 was a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded
dose-escalation study included a total of 72 treated patients with locally advanced and stage IV pancreatic cancer. The patients
received in this trial VXM01 or placebo (S. typhi carrying a non-coding DNA plasmid) in addition to gemcitabine as standard of care.
In addition to safety as primary endpoint, the VXM01-specific immune reaction, as well as clinical response parameters were
evaluated. After the initial doses, patients received up to six monthly boost vaccinations, or placebo treatment. Vaccinations were
applied orally, and concomitant treatment with standard-of-care gem-citabine during the priming phase (first 4 weekly doses):</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The effect gets more pronounced when looking at patients with successful
immune induction at prime:</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><img alt="" src="ea028315401_img10.jpg"/></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Observed pharmacodynamic effects in VXM01 treatment group vs. placebo
included</p><div>


</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; border-spacing: 0px;" width="100%"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 0.25in"/><td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&#9679;</span></td><td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">a decrease in tumor perfusion, </span></td></tr></table><div>

</div><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; border-spacing: 0px;" width="100%"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 0.25in"/><td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&#9679;</span></td><td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">increase in serum collagen, </span></td></tr></table><div>

</div><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; border-spacing: 0px;" width="100%"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 0.25in"/><td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&#9679;</span></td><td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">mild elevation in blood pressure, </span></td></tr></table><div>

</div><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; border-spacing: 0px;" width="100%"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 0.25in"/><td style="width: 0.25in"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&#9679;</span></td><td><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">mild drop in thrombo-cyte, leukocyte and lymphocyte counts. </span></td></tr></table><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">All of which are indictive of successful vessel targeting and ratification.
For example, increased blood pressure in patients treated with VXM01 over placebo indicates blood vessel rarefication.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Increase of VEGF-A and collagen IV (indicator of vessel destruction)
after vaccination further supported the observed vaccination effects on tumor perfusion, particularly since we observed a significant
inverse correlation between collagen IV serum levels and alterations of tumor perfusion after the vaccination.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">DCE-MRI was employed to assess tumor perfusion. After 38 days, tumor
perfusion as 18% reduced in the VXM01 subjects while unchanged in placebo treated patients</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">In conclusion, VXM01 elicits a productive, complex
VEGFR-2-specific effector T-cell response in patients with pancreatic cancer that correlates with anti- angiogenic activity and has
a favorable safety profile. Changes indicative of anti-angiogenic efficacy in tumor perfusion, serum biomarkers, and blood pressure
in VXM01 treated patients but not in the control arm were recorded.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Importantly, no safety concerns were noted</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

<td style="width: 0"/><td style="width: 0.25in"><b>2.</b></td><td><b>A phase1 clinical trial of VXM01 in Glioblastoma was initiated in May&#160;2016 (ClinicalTrials.gov ID:&#160;NCT02718443). The
trial was conducted at the Neurology Clinic and National Center for Tumor Diseases in Heidelberg, Germany, and the principal investigator
is Dr.&#160;Wolfgang Wick, MD, who is a professor at the Neurology Clinic and National Center for Tumor Diseases.</b></td></tr></table><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The phase&#160;I clinical trial was evaluated for 14 patients with
recurrent glioblastoma who had progressed after standard treatment and were candidates for reoperation. The primary objective of the study
was to examine the safety and tolerability of the investigational VEGFR2 DNA vaccine VXM01 after four vaccinations in glioblastoma patients.
The secondary objective was to examine the immune and biomarker response to the vaccine. During the course of this clinical trial, 7 patients
were alive and survived for more than 12&#160;months after initiation of treatment. No adverse effects related to VXM01 were observed.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">source: Wick, W et al. &#8220;P01.031 VXM01 phase&#160;I study in
patients with progressive glioblastoma&#160;&#8212;&#160;final results.&#8221; Neuro-Oncology&#160;vol.&#160;20, Suppl 3 (2018): iii235.
doi:10.1093/neuonc/noy139.073</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">As the Phase&#160;1 trial progressed, VXM01 was granted orphan drug
status by the FDA and EMA in 2017 for the treatment of glioma.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">As a next step, on November&#160;21, 2018, a combination study of VXM01
and anti-PD-L1&#160;checkpoint inhibitor avelumab in 28 patients with relapsed glioblastoma began (ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT03750071 ).
The trial included 25 patients with non-resectable&#160;tumors and 3 with resectable tumors. The main objective of the study is to evaluate
the safety and tolerability of VXM01 vaccine treatment in combination with avelumab.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Dr.&#160;Wolfgang Wick, the principal investigator for the Phase&#160;I
clinical trial and also a key opinion leader in the field of brain malignancies, also conducted this combination study. He will remain
principal investigator for future trials.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">This Phase&#160;I/II clinical trial was not sized or designed to yield
advanced comparative statistical results. Larger patient cohorts and additional design features typical of Phase&#160;2/PoC studies (including
randomization, Blinding, control groups) are required to obtain data yielding advanced statistics and guide the design of registrational
(Ph3) studies. Initiation of such trials is planned for 2026. That said, the data to date shows promising responses, including as single
agent, having generated considerable interest in the field at the time.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The study included 14 white patients with a mean age of 56.8&#160;years.
The majority of participants (64.3%) were male.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>VXM01 phase&#160;I clinical trial&#160;&#8212;&#160;Tumor response</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The tumor response was assessed by objective response rate (ORR) according
to immunotherapy Response Assessment for Neuro-Oncology&#160;(iRANO; 2015).</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Overall, the tumor response to VXM01 was mixed, with some patients
showing signs of stable disease or even tumor shrinkage, while others experienced disease progression. These findings highlight the variability
in treatment response and the challenges of managing glioblastoma. The extension study results provide further insights into the potential
for long-term&#160;disease control in some patients, but also underscore the need for further research to optimize treatment strategies
and identify those most likely to benefit.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: bottom">
    <td style="width: 32%; border-bottom: black 1.5pt solid"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Best Overall Response</b></span></td>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Note: A hyphen (-) indicates no events were reported. n = number
of patients with an event; N = number of patients; NR =&#160;non-resectable. Percentages are based on the number of patients. CR = complete
response; PR&#160;=&#160;partial remission; SD = stable disease; PD = progressive disease; ORR = objective response rate (CR and PR);
DCR = disease control rate (CR, PR, and SD).</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

</div><!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 20; Value: 1 --><div>
    </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->13<!-- Field: /Sequence --></p></div><div>
    </div><div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><p style="margin: 0pt"></p></div><div>
    </div><!-- Field: /Page --><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">In this study, we assessed clinical response using several measures,
including progression-free&#160;survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). PFS ranged from 9 to 366&#160;days, with a median PFS of 0.8&#160;months
in the 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU dose group and 2.6&#160;months in the 10<sup>6</sup>&#160;CFU dose group. OS ranged from 67 to 416&#160;days,
with a median OS of greater than 14&#160;months in the 10<sup>6</sup>&#160;CFU group and 7.6&#160;months in the 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU
group.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">For the 3 patients who entered the prolongation phase, PFS ranged between
30 and 960&#160;days, and overall survival ranged between 776 and 1147&#160;days. These findings suggest a potential advantage in terms
of PFS and OS for the lower dose group, although they may be influenced by the slightly better baseline status of the patients in the
10<sup>6</sup>&#160;CFU dose group.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>VXM01 phase&#160;1/2 clinical trial&#160;&#8212;&#160;Immune response</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The effect of VXM01 was explored by evaluating the VEGFR-2&#160;specific
T cell response and frequency of immune cells in peripheral blood, and by staining of immune- and biomarkers in tumor tissue obtained
during resection.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Peripheral&#160;T-cell&#160;response:</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">All 9 tested patients showed a VEGFR2-specific&#160;T-cell&#160;and
IFN-&#947;&#160;immune response, with a clear increase observed after the initial vaccination and further increases after the first booster
dose. This indicates that VXM01 effectively stimulated an immune response against VEGFR2, a protein involved in tumor growth.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">ELISpot assay was used to measure the number of these T cells that
produced interferon gamma (IFN-&#947;) when stimulated with different fragments of the VEGFR-2&#160;protein.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Brain Tumor Immunohistochemistry:</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">An analysis of tumor tissue from 8 re-operated&#160;patients showed
a statistically significant increase in CD8 T-cells&#160;(immune cells that kill cancer cells) after vaccination with VXM01. Specifically,
the mean number of CD8 T-cells&#160;increased from 159 cells/mm&#178; in the primary tumor to 296 cells/mm&#178; in the recurrent tumor,
with a P-value&#160;of 0.0239 (paired t-test). Additionally, there was a decrease in regulatory T-cells&#160;(Treg), which are immune
cells that suppress immune responses. The median number of Treg cells dropped from 32 cells/mm&#178; in the primary tumor to 12 cells/mm&#178;
in the recurrent tumor. This resulted in a higher CD8:Treg ratio, which has been associated with better clinical outcomes in other studies.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>VXM01 phase&#160;I clinical trial&#160;&#8212;&#160;Safety result</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">In this trial, there were no notable differences observed between the
two dose groups (10<sup>6</sup>&#160;CFU and 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU).</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">All patients experienced at least one treatment-emergent&#160;adverse
event (TEAE), but most were mild or moderate in severity and considered unrelated to VXM01. The most common TEAEs were consistent with
the underlying disease or progression of disease, and included aphasia, hemiparesis, fatigue, headache, and lymphopenia.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

</div><!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 21; Value: 1 --><div>
    </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->14<!-- Field: /Sequence --></p></div><div>
    </div><div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><p style="margin: 0pt"></p></div><div>
    </div><!-- Field: /Page --><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">No treatment-limiting&#160;toxicities (TLTs) were observed. Four TEAEs
(flatulence, dizziness, fatigue, and nausea) were considered related to VXM01, but all were mild and resolved without intervention. All
serious adverse events (SAEs) and deaths were attributed to the underlying disease or disease progression.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Note: A hyphen (-) indicates no events were reported. E = number
of events; n = number of patients with an event; N = number of patients. Percentages are based on the number of patients. CFU: colony
forming units.</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>VXM01 phase&#160;I/II clinical trial&#160;&#8212;&#160;Patient selection
criteria</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Patients were selected by a third party clinical trial provider, each
of whom met the following criteria:</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">With these criteria, the trial recruited 25 patients with non-resectable&#160;tumors
and 3 with resectable tumors. Overall, the mean age of participants was 58&#160;years, with the majority (78.6%) being male.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>VXM01 phase&#160;I/II clinical trial&#160;&#8212;&#160;Tumor response</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The tumor response was assessed by Objective Response Rate (ORR) and
Duration of Response (DoR) according to immunotherapy Response Assessment for Neuro-Oncology&#160;(iRANO; 2015)</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Overall, in the non-resectable&#160;patients the ORR was 12.0% (95%
CI: 2.5&#160;&#8211;&#160;31.2), with 3 responders out of 25&#160;patients (12.0%) who had a partial remission. Of the patients with a
partial remission, 1 patient in the 10<sup>6</sup>&#160;CFU/mL group had a DoR of 5.6&#160;months, while the patients in the 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL
group had a DoR of 2.7 and 11.1&#160;months. All patients who had stable disease (n=3) received 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL VXM01.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Note: A hyphen (-) indicates no events were reported. n = number
of patients with an event; N = number of patients; NR =&#160;non-resectable. Percentages are based on the number of patients. CR = complete
response; PR = partial remission; SD = stable disease; PD = progressive disease; ORR = objective response rate (CR and PR); DCR = disease
control rate (CR, PR, and SD).</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The clinical response was assessed by recurrence-free&#160;survival
after re-operation&#160;(RFS) (in the 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL resectable group), time-to-progression&#160;(TTP), progression free survival
(PFS), and overall survival (OS). In the patients who underwent tumor resection (10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL resectable group), disease
progression occurred only in Patient&#160;01-17&#160;with an RFS of 1.8. Patient&#160;01-14&#160;was censored with an RFS of 20.9&#160;months.
The results for TTP and PFS were identical, with an overall median of 2.7&#160;months and range of 1.2 to 13.8&#160;months in the non-resected&#160;patients
(Total NR group). The median OS in the Total NR group was 11.1&#160;months (95% CI: 8.5&#160;&#8211;&#160;15.1) with a range of 3.8 to
38.2&#160;months. At the time of database lock, 1 patient in the 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL resectable group was alive and had stable
disease without post-resection&#160;recurrence, while 3 patients in the 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL non-resectable&#160;group were alive
with progressive disease in longterm follow-up.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>VXM01 phase&#160;I/II clinical trial&#160;&#8212;&#160;Immune response</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The effect of VXM01 plus avelumab was explored by evaluating the VEGFR-2&#160;specific
T cell response and frequency of immune cells in peripheral blood, and by staining of immune- and biomarkers in tumor tissue obtained
during resection.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">ELISpot assay was used to measure the number of these T cells that
produced interferon gamma (IFN-&#947;) when stimulated with different fragments of the VEGFR-2&#160;protein.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">VEGFR-2&#160;specific ELISpot counts were calculated as the ELISpot
count per peptide pool minus the negative control. The VEGFR-2&#160;specific T cell response was defined positive when the test peptide
pool had at least two-fold&#160;higher spot counts compared to the negative control and the difference of the triplicates was significant
in an&#160;<i>unpaired&#160;two-tailed&#160;student&#8217;s&#160;t-test</i>.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Overall, 12 of 28 patients (42.9%, all in the 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL
non-resectable&#160;group) had a VEGFR-2&#160;specific T cell response classified as negative for all peptides at all time points tested.
The VEGFR-2&#160;specific T cell response was decreased on Day 21 compared with baseline in 6 patients, was increased in 4 patients (all
10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL non-resectable&#160;group), and remained at the same level compared with baseline in 5 patients. At Week&#160;16,
the VEGFR-2&#160;specific T cell response was increased compared with baseline in 7 patients (1 patient in 10<sup>6</sup>&#160;CFU/mL
group, 6 patients in 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL group), decreased in 5 patients (all 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL group), and remained the
same in 3 patients.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>VXM01 phase&#160;I/II clinical trial&#160;&#8212;&#160;Safety result</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The majority of reported events in this trial being mild to moderate
severity in nature but would need to be assessed in a larger patient population. Notably, while SAEs were observed during the study period,
all of them were target disease-related&#160;rather than treatment-related. The observed SAEs included brain edema, epilepsy, stroke,
hyponatremia, gait disturbance, and pulmonary embolism, which are commonly reported symptoms in patients with brain tumors or severe illnesses
as their disease progresses and were not attributable to VXM01 administration. A safety evaluation will be determined following review
of all safety data by relevant regulatory agencies.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

</div><!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 23; Value: 1 --><div>
    </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->16<!-- Field: /Sequence --></p></div><div>
    </div><div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><p style="margin: 0pt"></p></div><div>
    </div><!-- Field: /Page --><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">All patients (n=28; 100%) experienced multiple AEs, but no treatment-limiting&#160;toxicities
(TLT) related to VXM01 or avelumab, or infusion-related&#160;adverse events (AEs) were recorded for any group. No treatment-related&#160;SAEs
were recorded for the 10<sup>6</sup>&#160;CFU/mL and 10<sup>7</sup>&#160;CFU/mL resectable groups. No VXM01- or avelumab-related&#160;SAEs
or treatment-emergent&#160;SAEs were recorded for any group. One patient discontinued study treatment due to rheumatoid arthritis which
occurred after the first 5&#160;weeks of treatment. This adverse event was assessed as unrelated to VXM01 administration and occurred
independently of the patient&#8217;s underlying condition, thus it was not reported as TLT.&#160;Four patients experienced a total of
5&#160;(five) immune-related&#160;AEs (irAEs). These immune-related&#160;AEs included hypothyroidism, autoimmune thyroiditis, fatigue,
and the aforementioned rheumatoid arthritis. As with other reported events, these immune-related&#160;AEs were assessed and determined
to be unrelated to VXM01 administration.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Darnatein</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Corporate Overview</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Darnatein is developing design-augmented&#160;(DA) biologics for age-related&#160;and
other degenerative diseases, such as osteoarthritis and spine and joint disorders. Darnatein&#8217;s lead DA biologics are intended to
be injected directly into pathological tissues to promote regeneration of target tissues such as bone or cartilage cells. Leveraging these
innovative DA biologics to regenerate bone and cartilage has the potential to restore functionality and reduce pain across several degenerative
conditions.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Darnatein has identified and advanced two therapeutic candidates, DRT-102,
a clinical-stage&#160;asset for spinal fusion, and DRT-101, a pre-clinical&#160;stage asset for osteoarthritis. A small exploratory, clinical
trial of 15 patients with DRT-102&#160;indicated potential efficacy compared to a placebo, with no serious adverse events reported. Safety
and efficacy evaluation will be determined following review of all safety data by relevant regulatory agencies. Larger clinical trials
will be required to provide more extensive and accurate data on the safety and effectiveness of DRT102. A pre-clinical&#160;(non-human)
trial of DRT-101&#160;demonstrated cartilage regeneration and joint healing in animals, with no serious adverse events reported. Based
on these preliminary results, Darnatein intends to continue the development and testing of DRT-101&#160;and, when additional resources
are available, DRT-102. Darnatein has not previously advanced any therapeutic candidates into late-stage&#160;clinical trials nor received
regulatory and marketing approvals for any commercial sales of its products.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Opportunity</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Age-related&#160;degeneration, such as osteoarthritis and spine disorders,
is a naturally occurring process that may be accelerated due to chronic and cumulative impact over time. Limited therapeutic options exist
and only offer limited and temporary symptomatic relief with no cure currently available.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Beyond therapeutic options, invasive surgical procedures may be available
for spine and joint disorders but are not readily accessible and may not be a curative, pain-free, long-term&#160;solution. Additionally,
neither symptomatic therapies nor invasive and costly surgical procedures address the underlying cause of chronic and age-related&#160;degenerative
diseases. Darnatein&#8217;s novel Design Augmented (DA) approach has the potential to overcome these limitations of spine and joint disorders
and osteoarthritis with a regenerative therapy to overcome degeneration in bone and cartilage.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

</div><!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 27; Value: 1 --><div>
    </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->20<!-- Field: /Sequence --></p></div><div>
    </div><div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><p style="margin: 0pt"></p></div><div>
    </div><!-- Field: /Page --><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Design-Augmented&#160;Biologics Program</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">In recent&#160;years, scientists have studied the role of bone morphogenetic
proteins (BMPs) in healing bone and cartilage. BMPs have been used clinically in orthopedic procedures but they are typically administered
at high, supra-physiological&#160;concentrations that have been linked to undesirable local and systemic side effects. BMPs engineered
to have enhanced therapeutic potency may circumvent this problem and provide the desired effects of healing bone and cartilage while minimizing
the likelihood of adverse events.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 24pt">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>DRT-101&#160;for Cartilage and Joint Recovery</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">DRT-101&#160;is a synthetic bio-signaling&#160;molecule that replaces
BMPRII-binding&#160;segments of BMP-7, one of the bone-forming&#160;proteins, with high affinity ActRII binding segments of Activin A,
a member of the transforming growth factor &#223; (TGF-&#223;). In nature, endogenous BMP7 promotes chondrogenesis in damaged cartilage
tissue by signaling primarily via the type&#160;II receptor BMPRII and to a lesser extent via the activin type&#160;II receptor ActRII,
which it binds with lower affinity. DRT-101&#160;amplifies intracellular regeneration signaling capacity compared to natural BMP-7&#160;and
allows for regeneration and restoration of mechanically depleted cartilage cells to normal levels.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>DRT-101&#160;pre-clinical&#160;study in animals</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">DRT-101&#160;was evaluated in Sprague Dawley rats by ChemOn Inc. in
2021 for toxicity measurement. This study was conducted to assess the approximate lethal dose (ALD) and the dose-range&#160;finding(DRF)
of the test substance DRT-101, when administered intravenously.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The table below lists the type, species, purpose and results of our

GLP-licensed&#160;third-party&#160;vendor.</p><div>
